findings.title: Referer-based host check is the only guard and sets X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL
findings.body: The embeddable-host check relies solely on the client-supplied Referer header, which is trivial to spoof. Once it passes, the controller sets `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL`. The page can also be framed by any site that strips or forges the referer, which opens clickjacking. The check also compares only the host and ignores the scheme and port.

findings.title: Invalid ERB `end if` and nil topic in best view
findings.body: `<%- end if %>` is a syntax error in ERB: `end` is followed by a dangling `if` with no condition. The template will not compile, so `/embed/best` fails whenever a topic exists. Separately, the view uses `@topic_view.topic.url`. The `TopicView.new` call can raise if the topic is not visible to the user.

findings.title: Unescaped request.referer interpolated into inline JavaScript
findings.body: `'<%= request.referer %>'` is HTML-escaped but not JS-escaped. A referer containing `'`, a backslash, or a newline, or `</script>`-style content, breaks out of the string literal or the script block. The result is an XSS vector, or at minimum a broken postMessage target. It should use `j`/`to_json`. An empty referer also makes postMessage throw.

findings.title: `contents <<` mutates caller's string and the hash changes on every poll
findings.body: `contents <<` mutates the argument in place. It will raise `FrozenError` for frozen strings and has side effects for callers. The appended footer is included in the SHA1, which is acceptable only if it is deterministic. The footer also interpolates the URL into an `href='...'` without escaping.

findings.title: Kernel#open on admin-supplied URL and unsafe feed handling
findings.body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with open-uri's Kernel#open will execute a shell command if the string starts with `|`. It also reads local files. Use `URI.parse(url).open` or RestClient. The same applies to `open(url)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, where the URL comes from the embed_url request param (only host-checked in TopicRetriever).

findings.title: Feed item content handling can crash or import unsanitized HTML
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when an item has no content, aborting the whole poll. `CGI.unescapeHTML` is applied to the content. The result is imported as raw HTML (cook_method raw_html, validations skipped) and rendered with `raw post.cooked` in the embed view. No sanitization is applied, so a malicious or compromised feed can inject scripts. The unused `feed_key`, which was meant for modified-tracking, indicates unfinished logic.

findings.title: Non-atomic create can fail on unique index race and orphan data
findings.body: If `creator.create` fails, `post` is a post with errors and `present?` is true. The code then calls `TopicEmbed.create!` with `post.topic_id`, which may be nil, and raises on the NOT NULL column. Concurrent imports of the same URL (poll job plus retrieve job) can also both pass the `embed.blank?` check and violate the unique index, leaving an orphan topic. `PostCreator` has its own inner transaction that does not roll back the topic when the outer `create!` raises unless nested properly.

findings.title: absolutize_urls mishandles protocol-relative URLs and ports
findings.body: `start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.jpg`. These are rewritten into `http://host/cdn.example.com/x.jpg`, which is wrong. Relative paths without a leading slash (e.g. `foo.html`) are not handled at all. The prefix also omits the port for any URL on 80/443 regardless of scheme.

findings.title: Weak origin check in postMessage handler
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring check. An origin like `http://a` or an empty string would match as a substring of the Discourse URL, so an attacker origin that is a substring of discourseUrl is accepted. It should compare for equality against the parsed origin.

findings.title: Controller spec expects TopicRetriever.new in controller but controller enqueues a job
findings.body: The controller calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders 'loading'. The spec 'tells the topic retriever to work' expects `TopicRetriever.new` and `retrieve` to be called synchronously. That only passes if jobs run inline in test. The spec is also loose, since no render assertion is made. Separately, enqueuing a job on every uncached request for an arbitrary `embed_url` (the throttle only applies inside the job) allows queue flooding.

findings.title: Editing an existing migration to add force: true drops table data
findings.body: Modifying an already-shipped migration to add `force: true` makes `create_table` drop an existing `top_topics` table. The change is unrelated to this PR. The same applies to the `topic_embeds` migration, where `force: true` can silently drop data on re-run. Related, the unrelated whitespace edit to `MigrateWordCounts` (and its removed trailing newline) adds noise.

findings.title: Revised raw_html post cook behavior and skip_validations side effects
findings.body: `before_save` re-cooks via `cook`, which returns raw for raw_html posts. That works, but `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` now ignores the failure result as before. The `revise!` method still returns true even if save fails. `TopicEmbed.import` then does `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...)` regardless of whether the revision succeeded, so a failed revise marks the content as already synced.

findings.title: Reload loop via 30s timer with no retry limit
findings.body: The loading page reloads every 30 seconds forever. Each reload enqueues another retrieve job, hitting the Redis throttle. If the retrieval permanently fails (remote down, invalid user), the iframe loops indefinitely and generates load.
